facts.statement: Patagopelta was an extinct ankylosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the upper Campanian to lower Maastrichtian ages.
facts.quote: Patagopelta (meaning "Patagonian shield") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (upper Campanian–lower Maastrichtian) Allen Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Patagopelta were discovered in the Allen Formation at the Salitral Moreno locality near General Roca in the Río Negro Province of Argentina.
facts.quote: The Patagopelta fossil material was found in sediments of the Allen Formation (Salitral Moreno locality) near General Roca, Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Patagopelta cristata was formally described as a new genus and species in 2022 by a team of researchers including Facundo Riguetti and Victoria Arbour.
facts.quote: New remains described in 2022 allowed Patagopelta cristata to be described as a new genus and species of nodosaurine dinosaurs by Facundo Riguetti, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola, Denis Ponce, Leonardo Salgado, Sebastián Apesteguía, Sebastián Rozadilla, and Victoria Arbour.

facts.statement: A femur fossil of Patagopelta has been found with a length of only 25 centimeters.
facts.quote: Un fémur encontrado tiene una longitud de solo 25 centímetros.

facts.statement: Patagopelta is distinguished by high crests on the lateral elements of its neck osteoderms and a high crest on the anterior part of its femur.
facts.quote: Patagopelta se distingue por altas crestas en los elementos laterales de las placas del cuello y una cresta alta, el borde de un grupo de músculos, en la parte anterior del fémur.

facts.statement: Although originally classified within the family Nodosauridae, later evidence suggested Patagopelta belonged to the Parankylosauria.
facts.quote: While originally described as a member of the family Nodosauridae, later discoveries provided support for parankylosaurian affinities.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Patagopelta is a nodosaurid or a parankylosaurian, with 2024 studies suggesting affinities with parankylosaurs like Antarctopelta.
facts.quote: A study published in 2024 by Agnolín and colleagues reviewed vertebrate fossils from the Cerro Fortaleza Formation and similar Patagonian formations. They mentioned new findings that suggest that Patagopelta may actually represent a parankylosaurian, similar to ankylosaurs like Antarctopelta rather than nodosaurids.

facts.statement: Patagopelta possessed a distinctive frond-like tail weapon, similar to those seen in related parankylosaur genera.
facts.quote: It also has the distinctive frond-like 'macuahuitl' tail weapon seen in these genera.

facts.statement: New material suggests that Patagopelta was more heavily armored, robustly built, and larger than the related parankylosaurs Stegouros and Antarctopelta.
facts.quote: This new material—assuming it all belongs to Patagopelta—indicates it is more heavily armored, more robustly built, and larger in size than the related parankylosaurs Stegouros and Antarctopelta.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Patagopelta come from the Allen Formation in Argentina and are known from partial skeletons.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles provienen de la Formación Allen en Argentina y es conocido a partir de un esqueleto parcial.

facts.statement: Patagopelta is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: †Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Fossils of Patagopelta were discovered in the Allen Formation at Salitral Moreno near General Roca in the Río Negro Province of Argentina.
facts.quote: El material fósil de Patagopelta fue encontrado en sedimentos de la Formación Allen, en la localidad Salitral Moreno, cerca de General Roca, Provincia de Río Negro, Argentina.

facts.statement: The Patagopelta fossils date from the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Esta localidad data del Campaniense superior al Maastrichtiense inferior del período Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: Initial remains were described in 1996 and were frequently referred to in literature as the "Argentine ankylosaur".
facts.quote: Los primeros restos fueron descritos en 1996 y aparecían a menudo en la literatura como el "anquilosaurio argentino".

facts.statement: In 2022, new remains allowed Patagopelta cristata to be described as a new genus and species of nodosaurine dinosaur by Facundo Riguetti, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola, Denis Ponce, Leonardo Salgado, Sebastián Apesteguía, Sebastián Rozadilla, and Victoria Arbour.
facts.quote: Nuevos restos descritos en 2022 permitieron que Patagopelta cristata fuera descrito como un nuevo género y especie de dinosaurio nodosaurinos por Facundo Riguetti, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola, Denis Ponce, Leonardo Salgado, Sebastián Apesteguía, Sebastián Rozadilla y Victoria Arbour.

facts.statement: The generic name "Patagopelta" is derived from "Patago," referencing its discovery in Argentine Patagonia, and the Greek word "pelta," meaning "shield."
facts.quote: El nombre genérico, "Patagopelta", se deriva de "Patago", en referencia al descubrimiento del taxón en la Patagonia argentina, y de la palabra griega "pelta", que significa "escudo".

facts.statement: The specific name "cristata" means "crested" in Latin, referring to the large crests on its cervical osteoderms and femur.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, "cristata", significa "con cresta" en latín, en referencia a las grandes crestas en sus osteodermos cervicales y fémur.

facts.statement: Riguetti et al. (2022) recovered Patagopelta as a member of Nodosaurinae, contrasting with previous analyses that placed it in Panoplosaurini.
facts.quote: En sus análisis filogenéticos, Riguetti et al. (2022) recuperó a Patagopelta como miembro de Nodosaurinae, dentro de un clado de nodosáuridos enteramente norteamericanos de mediados del período Cretácico, en contraste con análisis previos que lo recuperaron en los Panoplosaurini.

facts.statement: The placement of Patagopelta suggests that nodosaurids were part of a migration event of North American fauna to South America.
facts.quote: En cualquier caso, sugiere que los nodosáuridos fueron parte de un evento de migración de la fauna de América del Norte hacia América del Sur.

facts.statement: Patagopelta belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Patagopelta is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Patagopelta lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Patagopelta has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: Patagopelta shared its habitat with birds like Lamarqueavis and Limenavis, pterosaurs like Aerotitan, rhynchosaurs like Lamarquesaurus, plesiosaurs like Kawanectes, and mammals like dryolesteoids and gondwanatherians.
facts.quote: Además compartía la formación con aves como Lamarqueavis y Limenavis, pterosaurios como Aerotitan, rincocéfalos como Lamarquesaurus, plesiosaurios como Kawanectes, y mamíferos dryolesteoides y gondwanaterios.

facts.statement: Agnolín et al. (2026) reported new fossil material supporting the placement of Patagopelta within Parankylosauria.
facts.quote: Agnolín et al. (2026) report the discovery of new fossil material of Patagopelta cristata, providing new information on the anatomy of members of this species and supporting its placement within Parankylosauria.
